 EPFO marks 74 years emphasising trust, service and worker welfare 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 1 November 2026, 4:52 pm 
 4 min read
 1 Nov 2026 
 ANI Photo | EPFO marks 74 years emphasising trust, service and worker welfare 
 The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) celebrated its 74th Foundation Day at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre in New Delhi, highlighting its evolution from a statutory provident fund entity to one of India’s leading social security institutions. The event underscored EPFO’s commitment to technology-enabled service delivery, compassionate governance, and the welfare of millions of workers and pensioners.
 Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, Mansukh Mandaviya, noted that EPFO has earned the trust of the country’s workforce over its 74-year history. He stated that this trust is exemplified by the organisation’s corpus of ₹32 lakh crore, built through contributions from over eight crore members, facilitated by the hard work and dedication of EPFO staff.

 Mandaviya emphasised the importance of social security being driven by human sensitivity, saying, “Every concern and grievance of workers must be addressed with compassion and empathy, viewing each worker with the respect and dignity they deserve as nation-builders.” He praised technological advancements such as CITES 2.01 and urged officials to prioritise worker welfare at the last mile.
 The Minister encouraged officials to draw inspiration from the ‘Panch Pran’ articulated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, stating, “Seva is our sanskaar,” and called on them to contribute towards the goal of Viksit Bharat. He also stressed the importance of worker-centric innovations as EPFO approaches its 75th year, encouraging adaptation and resilience in line with changing times. He extended Diwali greetings, wishing success and prosperity to all EPFO officials, members, and beneficiaries.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Chandra Bhushan Kumar, Secretary of the Ministry of Labour & Employment, reflected on EPFO’s role over more than seven decades in laying the foundation and strengthening India’s social security framework. He described it as a model for future generations and highlighted the need to extend social protection and labour reforms beyond the organised sector to unorganised workers. Kumar remarked that EPFO exemplifies achieving this reach through institutionalised processes.
 He added, “Reform is a continuous process and requires constant evolution in the current digital age in order to effectively solve the common man’s problems.” Kumar urged officials involved with reforms to adjust their mindset accordingly, emphasising the need for accessibility and ease of living for beneficiaries as part of collective efforts towards Viksit Bharat @2047.
 The Central Provident Fund Commissioner recounted EPFO’s journey from its founding in 1952 to serving approximately eight crore contributory members and 85 lakh pensioners, managing a retirement corpus nearing ₹32 lakh crore. He acknowledged the contribution of officers and employees nationwide who sustained service delivery amid significant technological and administrative changes.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 He stressed the importance of making EPFO more accessible, reliable, and humane, stating, “Institutional trust is built through every claim settled, every pension delivered and every family supported during difficult times.” He said the ultimate measure of EPFO’s success is the confidence and security felt by members and pensioners.
 The event showcased the impact of the technological transformation through CITES 2.01, highlighting that the average claim settlement time reduced to 2.57 days in October 2026, reflecting efforts to make provident fund access faster and more convenient.
 EPFO subscribers will soon be able to access their PF balance, recent transactions, and passbook information via EPFO’s verified WhatsApp service, which will also provide personalised guidance for PMVBRY-related requirements. This aims to improve service accessibility through a familiar mobile platform, reducing the need for office visits.
 Subscribers with Aadhaar-verified inoperative EPF accounts holding balances up to ₹1,000 will no longer need to file individual claims, as EPFO will automatically initiate settlements following identity and bank-account verification. Approximately 100,000 accounts with ₹5 crore in total are expected to benefit from this initiative.
 The 74th Foundation Day reaffirmed a shared vision that EPFO’s transformation must enhance security, dignity, and confidence for every worker and pensioner. The organisation aims to combine technological progress with human sensitivity, broaden social security coverage with dependable service, and pair institutional efficiency with compassionate governance.
 EPFO’s journey represents a sustained commitment to ensuring workers’ years of labour translate into security, dignity, and peace of mind for workers and their families.
 Also present were Chandra Bhushan Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment; Ramesh Krishnamurthi, Central Provident Fund Commissioner; members of the Central Board of Trustees; workers; employers; and other stakeholders.
